question: What do Breadchain Cooperative's (Bread Cooperative's) deployed contracts, source code, documentation, and on-chain state establish about its mechanisms, scale, governance, admin control, failure modes, and what it does not do, as of 2026-10-08?

frame.population: Breadchain Cooperative / Bread Cooperative and its BreadchainCoop GitHub organisation, Gnosis Chain deployments, and sibling deployments
frame.exposure: contract source in the repositories, verified deployed contracts, first-party docs, ClaimedYield logs, DeFiLlama
frame.comparator: a cooperative, non-custodial, yield-routing, credit-issuing protocol

findings.finding: BREAD is an upgradeable ERC20Votes token minted 1:1 against xDAI, wrapped to wxDAI and deposited into the sDAI vault; burn withdraws the exact amount from sDAI and returns native xDAI. The contract takes no fee and has no redemption delay.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: function burn(uint256 amount, address receiver) external { ... _burn(msg.sender, amount); sexyDai.withdraw(amount, address(this), address(this)); wxDai.withdraw(amount); _nativeTransfer(receiver, amount);

findings.finding: Yield is the sDAI position's asset value minus total BREAD supply; claimYield(amount, receiver) can be called only by the owner or the yieldClaimer address and mints new BREAD to the receiver, bounded by accrued yield.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint256 assets = sexyDai.convertToAssets(bal); uint256 supply = totalSupply(); return assets > supply ? assets - supply : 0;

findings.finding: The owner can set the yieldClaimer, rescue any token except the sDAI collateral, and (through the EIP173 proxy) upgrade the implementation. Every mint and transfer self-delegates the recipient's votes if they have no delegate.

No rule exists in the contract for a shortfall: if sDAI assets fall below BREAD supply, burn pulls the exact amount from sDAI and reverts when the vault cannot supply it, so the last redeemers bear the loss.

The repository contains one audit file: a pro bono review of Bread.sol by two KebabSec members, dated 2025-03-10 in the file name, with three findings (two informational, one low: claimYield clears the delegation of the yield recipient).

Voting power is the integral of a holder's BREAD (plus ButteredBread) checkpoint balance times blocks over the PREVIOUS cycle window [previousCycleStartingBlock, lastClaimedBlockNumber]. The raw sum is returned undivided by the block count.

A voter allocates integer points to each project (each at most maxPoints); the voter's power is split across projects in proportion to points over total points. Recasting within a cycle replaces the earlier allocation. Voting happens only against power earned in the earlier cycle, so a deposit made now cannot vote until the next cycle.

Distribution: balance = BREAD held by the distributor after claiming all accrued yield; fixed = balance / yieldFixedSplitDivisor, divided equally among projects; the remainder is split by vote weight. distributeYield() and distributeYieldGK() have no access control; they revert unless resolveYieldDistribution() is true (currentVotes > 0, at least cycleLength blocks since the last distribution, and enough yield for each project).

The owner alone queues project additions and removals (applied at the next distribution), and sets maxPoints, cycleLength, yieldFixedSplitDivisor, the ButteredBread address, and the Gas Killer AVS and BLS checker addresses. The contract is a proxy-upgradeable Ownable2Step contract. Membership of the recipient set is therefore not a vote of BREAD holders.

Optional voting multipliers: VotingStreakMultiplier adds multiplierIncrement per consecutive cycle voted up to maxMultiplierIncrements and lapses after two cycles of silence; NFTMultiplier and PermanentNFTMultiplier add a bonus for NFT holders. Multiplier bonuses add (factor minus 1x) to a 1x base.

ButteredBread is a non-transferable ERC20Votes token minted when a holder deposits an allowlisted LP token; minted amount is deposit times scalingFactor / 100, the owner can change scaling factors and the allowlist, and delegation is forced to follow the BREAD delegate.
The Gas Killer SDK (an EigenLayer AVS for off-chain tallying) is wired into the distributor via the trackState modifier and distributeYieldGK().

item.title: BreadchainCoop/saving-circles: SavingCircles, GoalSavingCircles, AutomaticSavingCircles (commit 2026-10-05, release v1.1.0)

findings.finding: SavingCircles is a plain ROSCA on an allowlisted ERC20: 2 to 25 members, a fixed depositAmount per interval, and the pot of depositAmount times member count paid to the member whose index equals the current round; payout order is the order in which members joined (owner first). It charges no interest, runs no auction, and takes no collateral.

If a round's deposits are incomplete after its end, any member can decommission the circle; the contract returns deposits that sit in the rounds of members who have not yet claimed, and a member who already claimed keeps the pot received. No bond, penalty, or pricing of an early position exists in the contract.

Invites are EIP-712 signatures by the circle owner; the owner controls the start; the contract owner (an Ownable proxy admin) sets allowed tokens. A Celo deploy script uses USDT, and the front-end app serves Gnosis and Celo (MiniPay).

GoalSavingCircles (added in v1.1.0, 2026-10-05) locks member deposits toward a goalAmount by a deadline and then releases the pot to a beneficiary or lets members withdraw; its design note states it has no credit, no interest, no auctions and no rounds. AutomaticSavingCircles lets an executor address trigger members' pre-authorized deposits and claims.

findings.finding: Safety Net implements a Broodfonds-style mutual: members pay a fixed monthly deposit; the pool is credited the deposit and the member's withdrawable balance is credited deposit times the redeem ratio (configurable 1 to 25). Above ratio 1 the excess is a claim on the shared pool.

getEffectiveRedeemRatio throttles the ratio actuarially: the cap is 1 / (p + z * sqrt(p(1-p)/N)) with p = 2% sick share and z = 1.65 over N members, and a six-month pool-runway cap; withdrawals are requests that other members can contest within a window; on decommission any shortfall is settled pro rata.

The current Gnosis stack was deployed 2026-07-04 (block 47031243): proxy 0x63c3c299CD5C5479E6999189D7827490Ea71cEAe, implementation 0x7763be733f595C3AB7dEE713937f0c2F116acE21, ProxyAdmin 0x83909C3dd3734f8575b65CD2F6bEda63A696d26F, allowed tokens WXDAI and BREAD. findings.finding: crowdstake.fun generalizes Bread into a factory framework: CrowdStakeFactory deploys CREATE2 beacon proxies from an allowlist of beacons; yield tokens wrap any ERC-4626 vault (StableYield) or sDAI (SexyDaiYield); pluggable cycle, voting (basis-points, cross-chain votes via signature, streak NFT), recipient-registry (admin or voting), distribution-strategy (equal or voted), and Chainlink/Gelato automation modules.
TimeWeightedVotingPower averages a holder's checkpoint balance over the CURRENT cycle so far, in contrast with Bread's previous-cycle window.

A live Gnosis instance is listed with token CSTAKE 0x7E94a840143E3D5C78f367bBe45e6fB6e55098ec, distribution manager 0xB38B15ad418202D3FdC1A139cEc51A8c13f59CB6, cycle module 0xDfBDa0C7061276C3B8a08aC38fEdeE63c0B63827, voting module 0xf921AF0C0fCd4A9dE0F6C58b34b05DBCCf0aAc42.

The O.U.R.COOP fork (an artists' cooperative in the Shared Visions program, co-funded by the European Union) adds a cUSD yield token, a project registry with budgets, a 100-point one-person-one-vote module, and a top-N art-fund strategy.

CoopStable runs on Stellar Soroban: users deposit USDC and receive cUSD 1:1; the lending yield controller routes the collateral to Blend Capital; the yield distributor sends 10% (configurable) to a treasury and splits 90% equally among members each epoch (24 hours by default). There is no vote in this design.

Mainnet contract ids are listed in mainnet.contracts.json, including cUSD CA7JSNCTAGTVXJJX65YIN53XAXK72NZPD5Q62YUQXV7R7V45ELKONCJ5 and the yield distributor CA2BNJFVCRJWCWLLOMJ3E3A62XMZ43U4K7RC6WVBOFC7RPYOJAH5BJVH.

item.title: Stellar Expert asset record for Coopstable cUSD

findings.finding: On 2026-10-08 the cUSD asset shows supply 152539830 base units (seven decimals, 15.25 cUSD), 7 trustlines of which 3 funded, 12 payments, created 2025-07-17.

Each monthly distribution is divided into two equal halves: the first split evenly across member projects regardless of the vote, the second by token vote, one BREAD one vote, with voting power from the average BREAD held over the previous month.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Each monthly distribution is divided into two equal halves.

findings.finding: The Operational Annex lists seven member projects (Bread Core Team, Symbiota, Regen Coordination, Crypto Commons Association, Citizen Wallet, Gardens, Traditional Dream Factory); new projects require a unanimous vote of the whole group, removal a majority vote after two sessions and a month to cure. The shared treasury Safe is gno:0x6A148b997e6651237F2fCfc9E30330a6480519f0 with one representative per member project; the core-team Safe is gno:0x918dEf5d593F46735f74F9E2B280Fe51AF3A99ad.
Member projects must hold at least 3,000 BREAD in their treasuries, join monthly calls, and be in a multisig; the page that lists these expectations is marked draft.

Bread Cooperative describes itself as worker-owned with no CEO and no outside shareholders and offers contract development (smart contracts, EigenLayer AVS architecture, democratic treasury systems, community currency infrastructure) at contact@bread.coop.

Stacks is documented as savings circles with no bank, no lender and no interest; companies and individuals can provide matching funds on completed circles. The Constitution names four principles: Economic Democracy, Mutual Aid, Transparent Governance, Dual Power.
